title: Málaga March Against Gender-Based Violence

tea.why: Protesters marched in Málaga on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women to oppose gender-based violence.
tea.want: Participants demanded an end to gender-based violence and greater protection and rights for women.
tea.changed: Nov 26: Sur in English reported that thousands demonstrated in Málaga city centre and heard a manifesto read by actress Adelfa Calvo.

summary: On 25 November 2026, the Violencia Cero platform organised a march in Málaga to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women under the slogan "A las violencias machistas no des like". The demonstration began at Plaza de la Merced and proceeded through the city centre to Plaza de la Constitución, where actress Adelfa Calvo read out the official manifesto. The mobilisation followed recent statistics highlighting Málaga as the Andalusian province with the highest number of gender-based murders for the year. According to sources, National Police estimated the crowd at over 1,000 participants, while organisers placed the figure at 3,000. Elected officials, including Mayor Francisco de la Torre, participated in the march.
demands: Eradication of all forms of gender-based violence
Promotion of a just and equal society
response: No official response reported in the sources.

crowd.text: more than 1,000 people according to the National Police, and 3,000 people according to Violencia Cero

updates.text: The Violencia Cero platform convened a march starting from Plaza de la Merced in Málaga.
Sur in English reported that protesters marched to Plaza de la Constitución, where actress Adelfa Calvo read the manifesto.
